tools.name: gate
tools.description: Call BEFORE buying a token on Robinhood Chain. Returns ALLOW, DENY or REVIEW, every check with the fact it read, and an EIP-712 signed receipt. Missing data never gives ALLOW unless the policy says so.

tools.name: gate_batch
tools.description: Gate up to 10 tokens against one policy in one call, one receipt each. Counts as one Gate call per token.

tools.name: gate_facts
tools.description: Every fact a policy rule may use (name, type, meaning), the rule syntax, the presets, and current pricing.

tools.name: get_receipt
tools.description: A stored decision receipt by id (rcpt_…).

tools.name: verify_receipt
tools.description: Checks that a receipt was signed by Actuary and that nothing in it changed. Pass the receipt object or its id.

tools.name: create_mandate
tools.description: For a token you hold: $0.05 per 7 days over x402 (pay via the REST API or the stdio MCP server). Re-checks a token against the policy about every 30 minutes. Changes (decision, owner, implementation, mint/pause/blacklist, supply) are recorded as events you poll with mandate_events; optionally also P

tools.name: mandate_signal
tools.description: The newest signed signal for a mandate: exit, watch or hold, from its last decision, valid for one hour. Verify it, then your own code decides whether to sell; Actuary never trades.

tools.name: verify_signal
tools.description: Checks that a mandate signal was signed by Actuary, that nothing in it changed and that it is still fresh. Act only on valid and fresh.

tools.name: mandate_events
tools.description: Events a mandate recorded since a unix time (0 = all). Use next_since for the following poll.

tools.name: mandate_status
tools.description: Current decision, delivery mode, last check and failures of a mandate.

tools.name: cancel_mandate
tools.description: Stops checks and events for a mandate, e.g. after selling the token.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_mandate" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: gate · Private data: gate, gate_batch, create_mandate, cancel_mandate · Public sink: create_mandate.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: gate · Private data: gate, gate_batch, create_mandate, cancel_mandate · Public sink: create_mandate

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
